info.long_name: ED Encounters with a Concussion Diagnosis
info.short_description: Monthly count of ED encounters with a concussion diagnosis (ICD-10-CA S06.0).
info.long_description: Monthly count of emergency department encounters with a concussion diagnosis, per Epic's "Concussion( ICD-10-CA: S06.0 )" ED Diagnoses grouping. Data from Epic Cosmos, which contains de-identified data from 300M+ patients across 1,600+ hospitals. Counts of 10 or fewer are suppressed by Epic and imputed as 5; see epic_n_concussion_suppressed_flag. Population base per SlicerDicer session 2852165: data model ED Encounters, population base All ED Encounters, criteria Country of Residence = United States of America - the denominator (epic_n_ed_encounters) is all ED encounters regardless of diagnosis. Stratified by age at time of visit and evaluated sex; age buckets are Epic's own (not the PopHIVE standard bands). As of the 2852165 export the buckets are contiguous (10-13 Years, 14-17 Years); an earlier export (session 2851311) used 10-12 Years and had a gap at age 13.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} ED encounters had a concussion diagnosis.

info.long_name: Total ED Encounters (Denominator)
info.short_description: Monthly total ED encounter count (any diagnosis), used as the denominator for the concussion percentage.
info.long_description: Monthly total count of ED encounters, regardless of diagnosis, used as the denominator for epic_pct_concussion. Data from Epic Cosmos SlicerDicer session 2852165 (ED Diagnoses = "Total" bucket). Counts of 10 or fewer are suppressed by Epic and imputed as 5; see epic_n_ed_encounters_suppressed_flag. Population base: All ED Encounters, Country of Residence = United States of America.

info.long_name: Percent of ED Encounters with a Concussion Diagnosis
info.short_description: Monthly percent of ED encounters with a concussion diagnosis (ICD-10-CA S06.0).
info.long_description: Monthly percentage of ED encounters with a concussion diagnosis, computed as epic_n_concussion / epic_n_ed_encounters * 100 - a percent of all ED encounters, NOT a rate per 100,000. Where the numerator was suppressed it is imputed as 5 before the percentage is computed. Where the denominator was itself suppressed the percentage is left missing, because dividing by the imputed denominator of 5 would assert a meaningless value; those cells are marked by epic_n_ed_encounters_suppressed_flag. Data from Epic Cosmos SlicerDicer. Population base per SlicerDicer session 2852165: data model ED Encounters, population base All ED Encounters, criteria Country of Residence = United States of America.
info.statement: In {location}, {value}% of ED encounters had a concussion diagnosis.

info.short_description: Primary measure value. Units vary by measure -- see the measure's own unit. Rows flagged suppressed do NOT carry a usable value; see that column.

1 if the source suppressed the estimate (a count of 10 or fewer, imputed as 5). epic_pct_concussion carries its numerator's flag; rows where the denominator (epic_n_ed_encounters) was suppressed are dropped entirely rather than computed from an imputed denominator. info.short_description: Always 'United States'. NEISS is a national probability sample of ~100 emergency departments and has no state breakdown.
Always '00' (national).
End of the treatment year the count covers (YYYY-12-31).
Calendar year of `time`, for convenience.

Completed months of age ('00 months' through '23 months') for the under-2s, then '2-4 years', '5-9 years', '10-14 years' and '15-19 years'. The levels are mutually exclusive and can be summed freely: NEISS also reports a coarse 'Under 2 years' band, but it is dropped here in favour of the 24 month rows that partition it. Under 20 only; NEISS 'Unknown' age and all adult bands are dropped.
'Male', 'Female' or 'Unknown' as reported by NEISS, plus 'All' -- a total that includes Unknown.
Primary NEISS diagnosis for the ED visit (e.g. 'Laceration', 'Fracture'). Only each cell's top 10 diagnoses are present, so the set varies from cell to cell; see `rank`.
Dashboard page this row belongs to. Always 'Injury and violence' in this file.
Topic grouping within the section. Always 'Injury diagnoses' in this file.
Data source the row came from. Always 'CPSC NEISS' in this file.

Rank of the diagnosis within its age x sex x year cell, 1 (most injuries) to 10. Ranked PER CELL, so the set of diagnoses varies from cell to cell -- a diagnosis missing from a cell fell outside that cell's top 10, which does not mean it was zero. Ranked on `value`, the weighted national estimate, which is not the same ordering as `n_sampled`: because NEISS weights vary by ED size stratum, a diagnosis with fewer sampled records can outrank one with more (10-14 years, all sexes, 2019: strain/sprain ranks above fracture on the national estimate despite fewer sampled records). Ties are broken by diagnosis name. Diagnoses with no sampled records are dropped rather than ranked, so a sparse cell can carry fewer than 10. The catch-all 'other or not stated' bucket is excluded from the ranking.

info.long_name: ED-treated injuries, weighted national estimate
info.short_description: Estimated number of ED-treated injuries nationally, from NEISS survey weights.
info.long_description: Sum of NEISS survey weights for the stratum, which scales the sampled records up to a national estimate of ED-treated injuries. This file carries only the weighted estimate, so there is no `measure` column. Read `n_sampled` alongside it as the sample size, or `unstable_flag` for the CPSC threshold below which an estimate is considered unstable.

info.short_description: `value` as a percent of ALL injuries in the same age x sex x year cell, on the weighted scale throughout -- i.e. what share of this group's ED injuries carried this diagnosis. The denominator is the summed weighted estimate over every diagnosis, including the excluded 'other or not stated' catch-all, which is large here, so the 10 retained percentages sum to well under 100 (median ~83, and as low as ~33 in the sparsest cells); the gap is the catch-all plus anything outside the top 10.
Raw count of NEISS sample records behind `value`. A sample size, NOT a national figure. CPSC guidance is that estimates built on fewer than 20 sampled records are unstable; see `unstable_flag`.

1 where `n_sampled` is below 20 -- the threshold under which CPSC considers a NEISS estimate unstable -- and 0 otherwise. Flagged rows are real estimates, not suppressed cells, and are kept as reported; treat them as indicative only. The flag fires on most single-month-of-age rows and rarely on the wider year bands, so filter on unstable_flag == 0 or mark the flagged points when plotting the month rows.

info.short_description: Percent of high school students who actually attempted suicide.
info.long_description: Weighted percentage of U.S. high school students who actually attempted suicide, from the CDC Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS) (topic: Unintentional Injuries and Violence; YRBSS question code: H29). Estimates are reported overall and stratified (separately) by sex, race/ethnicity, and grade; grade is mapped to approximate modal ages (9th=14, 10th=15, 11th=16, 12th=17). Missing estimates are set to 0 and flagged: pct_attempted_suicide_suppressed = 1 marks values CDC suppressed (e.g., small sample size), and pct_attempted_suicide_not_asked = 1 marks geography-years in which the question was not asked. Note: New York state estimates exclude New York City.

wisqars.name: Web-based Injury Statistics Query and Reporting System (WISQARS)
wisqars.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
wisqars.description: WISQARS (Web-based Injury Statistics Query and Reporting System) is an interactive, online database that provides fatal and nonfatal injury, violent death, and cost of injury data from a variety of trusted sources. Maintained by CDC's National Center for Injury Prevention and Control, WISQARS enables public health professionals and researchers to access injury-related mortality data from the National Vital Statistics System, nonfatal injury data from the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS), and violent death data from the National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS). Data are available at national and state levels for various injury mechanisms including motor vehicle crashes, falls, poisonings (including drug overdoses), firearms, and self-harm. WISQARS supports injury surveillance, research, and prevention program planning.
wisqars.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

nhtsa_fars.name: Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)
nhtsa_fars.location: NHTSA File Downloads — FARS National CSV archives
nhtsa_fars.description: FARS is a nationwide census providing NHTSA, Congress, and the American public with yearly data on fatal injuries suffered in motor vehicle traffic crashes. FARS contains data on all crashes in the United States involving a fatality in a motor vehicle traffic crash on a public road. A fatal crash is one in which a motor vehicle is involved and at least one person dies within 30 days of the crash. Data are collected from police crash reports, state vehicle registration files, state driver licensing files, state highway department data, vital statistics, and other sources. FARS has been operational since 1975 and covers all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico (national files cover the 50 states and DC).
nhtsa_fars.restrictions: Public domain. NHTSA data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

yrbss.name: CDC Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS)
yrbss.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
yrbss.description: The Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS) is a set of school-based surveys conducted by the CDC that monitor health-related behaviors among U.S. high school students. The biennial national, state, and local surveys provide weighted prevalence estimates of behaviors contributing to the leading causes of death and disability. Data were accessed via the YRBS Explorer API. Estimates are provided overall and stratified (separately, not crossed) by sex, race/ethnicity, and grade. Estimates that CDC suppressed (e.g., small sample sizes) are omitted rather than imputed. State estimates are available only for jurisdictions that share data with CDC; Minnesota, Oregon, and Washington are not included, and New York state excludes New York City.
yrbss.restrictions: Public domain. Suggested attribution: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS).

epic_cosmos.name: Epic Cosmos
epic_cosmos.description: Epic Cosmos is a collaborative research platform containing de-identified patient data from over 300 million patients across more than 1,600 hospitals and health systems using Epic electronic health record systems. Data is accessed via SlicerDicer, a self-service analytics tool. The dataset includes emergency department visits, diagnoses, immunizations, laboratory results, and other clinical data. Due to privacy protections, counts fewer than 10 are suppressed and imputed. Coverage extends across all U.S. states and territories. Note that county-level and city-level stratifications could differ markedly in total sample size due to high levels of missingness of county data in some states.
epic_cosmos.restrictions: The data can be re-used with appropriate attribution. A suggested citation relating to this data is 'Results of research performed with Epic Cosmos were obtained from the PopHIVE platform (https://github.com/PopHIVE/Ingest).'

medicaid_quality_cms.name: Medicaid and CHIP Adult and Child Core Set Quality Measures
medicaid_quality_cms.location: Medicaid.gov Open Data – Quality Measures datasets (2014–2023)
medicaid_quality_cms.description: Annual state-level performance data on the Medicaid and CHIP Adult Core Set and Child Core Set quality measures, as voluntarily reported by states to CMS and analyzed by Mathematica via the Quality Measure Reporting (QMR) system. Measures span behavioral health (e.g., follow-up after ED visits for mental illness, substance use disorder treatment), primary and preventive care (e.g., well-child visits, immunizations), maternal and perinatal health (e.g., prenatal and postpartum care, low birthweight), dental health, care of chronic conditions (e.g., diabetes, asthma, hypertension), and long-term services and supports. Each annual dataset includes state rates and national 25th and 75th percentile benchmarks. Data cover federal fiscal years 2014–2023. Reporting is voluntary; not all states report all measures each year. The wide-format standard file contains one row per state-year-payer-domain combination, with each measure-statistic combination as a separate column following the naming convention medicaid_{measure_abbr}_{population}_{sub_metric}_{stat} where population is 'ch' (child) or 'ad' (adult), sub_metric captures time windows or sub-components, and stat is 'rate', 'pct_25', or 'pct_75'.
medicaid_quality_cms.restrictions: Public domain. CMS/Medicaid.gov data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

chr.name: County Health Rankings & Roadmaps
chr.organization: University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute
chr.location: County Health Rankings & Roadmaps Annual Data
chr.description: The County Health Rankings & Roadmaps (CHR&R) program, a collaboration between the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation and the University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute, ranks the health of nearly all counties in the nation. The annual rankings measure vital health factors including high school graduation rates, obesity, smoking, unemployment, access to healthy foods, the quality of air and water, income inequality, and teen births that influence how long and how well we live. Data are released annually and cover all U.S. counties. Raw data are publicly available through the Zenodo repository (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18157681) and span release years 2010 through the present.
chr.restrictions: CC BY 4.0. Attribution required. Cite as: University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute. County Health Rankings & Roadmaps. https://www.countyhealthrankings.org.

noaa_wpc_heatrisk.name: NOAA WPC HeatRisk
noaa_wpc_heatrisk.description: The NOAA Weather Prediction Center HeatRisk product provides a daily, gridded (2.5 km) assessment of heat risk across the contiguous United States for the current day and 7-day forecast period. Risk is classified on a 0–4 scale based on the combination of heat intensity and duration relative to local historical thresholds, with consideration for overnight low temperatures and heat index. The archive provides daily GeoTIFF rasters back to August 1, 2024. County- and state-level summaries in this dataset are computed as the mean pixel value within each geographic boundary using area-weighted zonal statistics.
noaa_wpc_heatrisk.restrictions: Public domain. NOAA data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

nis.name: National Immunization Survey (NIS)
nis.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
nis.description: The National Immunization Surveys (NIS) are a group of telephone surveys used to monitor vaccination coverage among children 19-35 months, teens 13-17 years, flu vaccinations for children 6 months-17 years, and COVID-19 vaccination for children, teens, and adults. The surveys are sponsored and conducted by the National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases (NCIRD) of the CDC and authorized by the Public Health Service Act. NIS provides population-based, state and local area estimates of vaccination coverage using a standard survey methodology. Surveys collect data through telephone interviews with parents or guardians in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and some U.S. territories. Cell phone numbers are randomly selected and called to enroll age-eligible children. With parental permission, vaccination providers are contacted to verify immunization records. Children and teens are classified as up to date based on ACIP-recommended vaccine doses.
nis.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

SchoolVaxView.name: SchoolVaxView
SchoolVaxView.location: Vaccination Coverage and Exemptions among Kindergartners
SchoolVaxView.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
SchoolVaxView.description: SchoolVaxView monitors vaccination coverage among U.S. school-aged children. Data are collected annually by states, territories, and select local jurisdictions through school vaccination assessments, which review student vaccination records at kindergarten entry. These data are made available by the CDC.
SchoolVaxView.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

neiss.name: National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS)
neiss.location: NEISS public query / archived data files
neiss.description: NEISS is a national probability sample of hospital emergency departments (~100 of the ~5,000+ U.S. hospitals with 24-hour EDs) operated by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. Each sampled record describes an injury treated in the ED, including patient age, sex, race, Hispanic ethnicity (added 2019), diagnosis, body part, disposition, up to three associated consumer products, and a statistical weight (plus sampling stratum and PSU). Sample weights scale records to national estimates; raw record counts are not nationally representative. This bundle uses the annual national counts for 2019 onward, restricted to patients under 20 and aggregated over race and Hispanic ethnicity to age x sex x year. Product groups are reconstructed from NEISS product-code bands and are approximate, not an official CPSC taxonomy.
neiss.restrictions: Public domain. NEISS data are produced by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission and are generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

cdc_wonder_ucd_drowning.name: CDC WONDER Underlying Cause of Death, 2018-2024 (ICD-10, expanded)
cdc_wonder_ucd_drowning.organization: CDC National Center for Health Statistics
cdc_wonder_ucd_drowning.description: Mortality data from death certificates filed in the 50 states and the District of Columbia, queried through CDC WONDER's Underlying Cause of Death (ICD-10, expanded) database and restricted to unintentional drowning: ICD-10 codes W65 (bathtub), W66 (swimming pool fall), W67 (in swimming pool), W68 (fall into swimming pool), W69 (natural water), W70 (fall into natural water), W73 (other specified drowning/submersion), and W74 (unspecified drowning/submersion). Data are broken out separately by age group, sex, single race, and Hispanic origin (each queried independently, not cross-tabulated), at both the state and county level, for years 2018-2024. State and county both use CDC WONDER's Ten-Year Age Groups (<1, 1-4, 5-14, 15-24, ..., 85+), but the two levels differ in how population is sourced. At the state level, CDC WONDER reports Population and Crude Rate directly for Ten-Year Age Groups. At the county level, CDC WONDER reports Deaths only for this age variable -- Population and Crude Rate remain checked (mandatory) in the query form but the server omits them from the export regardless, for every state and year. County-level population is therefore derived here by summing CDC's Five-Year Age Groups county population export into the same Ten-Year buckets (e.g. 5-9 + 10-14 = 5-14); crude_rate is then recomputed from that derived population rather than taken from CDC directly, so drowning_crude_rate_lcl/_ucl are not populated for county-level age rows (a valid confidence interval needs CDC's own interval method, which this derivation does not replicate). This also surfaces a further CDC limitation: county-level population is reported as 'Not Applicable' for the <1, 1-4, and 85+ Five-Year groups nationwide, for every county regardless of size -- so missing_denom_flag = 1 for those three Ten-Year buckets at the county level essentially always, and county-level drowning rates (though not death counts) are structurally unavailable for infants/toddlers and the oldest age group. Suppressed death counts (1-9 deaths) are filled in with 5, the midpoint of the range, and the rate is recomputed from that count; suppressed_flag = 1 marks these estimated rows (confidence bounds stay -999), and a true zero is reported as 0. Values that cannot be computed are coded -999. suppressed_flag = 1 where CDC withheld a cell for confidentiality (any cell representing fewer than 10 deaths); this affects the death count and the rates derived from it, never the population. missing_denom_flag = 1 where no population denominator exists for that geography and demographic combination (CDC reports 'Not Applicable' or 'Not Available', or -- for county-level age specifically -- the Five-Year population export used to derive it was itself missing); this affects the population and the rates derived from it, never the death count. The two are not mutually exclusive and are both 1 on rows carrying both markers, which is common at the county level. National rows (geography 00, in data_state.csv.gz) come from separate CDC WONDER national queries (scrape_national.py) with the same breakdowns, not from summing the states: every state cell with fewer than 10 deaths is suppressed, so a sum of state counts undercounts (2024: 4,087 from the state cells vs 4,201 reported nationally). The all-ages Overall rows (age = Overall, sex and race Overall) at the national, state and county level are CDC WONDER's own totals from separate queries, not sums of other rows. Each geography also has an age = 0-24 row, a single WONDER query over ages 0-24 (national and state: Ten-Year groups <1, 1-4, 5-14, 15-24; county: the equivalent Five-Year groups, because CDC omits county population for Ten-Year groups), so a cell is suppressed only if all of 0-24 has 1-9 deaths. The 0-24 row overlaps the ten-year age rows, so do not sum across age.
